Target Coordinates                                   Lat 30.92357, Lon -97.90167



 BLUF (Bottom Line Up Front)
 Oncor secured an informal "no impact" concurrence from Fort Cavazos Airspace Command
 by providing deflated structure heights (140'–190') belonging to a smaller 345-kV system.
 Oncor’s own documentation admits this 765-kV project is engineered "up to just under 200
 feet" to exploit a statutory loophole and evade mandatory FAA Obstruction Evaluation (14 CFR
 § 77.9). This introduces unlit, 199-foot steel barricades directly into a low-level tactical
 rotary-wing training corridor, creating a fatal hazard for 1st Air Cavalry Brigade aviators.




 I. THE REGULATORY MANIPULATION
    ●​ The Misrepresentation: On March 18, Fort Cavazos Airspace Command evaluated the
          project based on Oncor's stated heights of 140 to 190 feet AGL.
    ●​ The Reality: Oncor's official FAQ admits the 190-foot specification applies to smaller
          345-kV lines, while the 765-kV structures for this project will be engineered "up to just
          under 200 feet".
    ●​ The Statutory Exploit (14 CFR § 77.9): Federal law mandates FAA aeronautical studies
          for structures 200 feet and higher. By designing to 199 feet, Oncor avoids automatic
          federal radar and obstruction lighting triggers while physically barricading military
          airspace.
    ●​ The Cover-Up: To conceal this strategy, Oncor subsequently redacted all "Maximum
       Structure Height" data for links nearest to Fort Cavazos in their public PUCT filings.
       Furthermore, Oncor omitted Page 1 of the DoD Clearinghouse review letter from their
       docket appendices.




II. THE TACTICAL AVIATION HAZARD
   ●​ The Airspace: The Briggs corridor contains a critical rotary-wing turnaround sector
       with a Military Training Route (MTR) floor of Surface-to-500 feet AGL.
   ●​ The Doctrine: Army Aviation Terrain Flight doctrine (Nap-of-the-Earth / Contour)
       requires pilots to operate routinely below 200 feet AGL.
   ●​ The Threat: Inserting a dense array of unlit, 199-foot steel lattice towers and static
       wire into this specific envelope physically severs the training corridor. During
       Degraded Visual Environments (DVE) or tactical brownout conditions, these unlit
       structures leave zero margin for pilot error.




III. REQUESTED FEDERAL ACTION
Fort Cavazos’s March 24th "no impact" determination is structurally invalid, as it was based
on misrepresented 345-kV height parameters. We formally request the immediate recension
of the informal review and the initiation of a binding, formal hazard assessment under 10
U.S.C. § 183a by the DoD Siting Clearinghouse.
